transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… it’s a bit embarrassing to say out loud, but I think I’m here because I’ve started arranging my life around not seeing spiders. Not just, you know, “I don’t like them” — I mean I’m changing what I do in my own house.

I put off doing laundry if it means going down to the basement, and I’ll avoid the garden shed even when I need something perfectly ordinary from it. And then I end up paying someone to do little jobs that I absolutely know how to do myself, just because I can’t make myself go into those spaces where I might see one. It feels ridiculous, especially because I’m a grown woman and I manage a classroom full of teenagers for a living, but at home I’m sort of planning everything around avoiding them.
When you actually see a spider, do you feel a sudden surge of intense fear?

Yes—very sudden. It’s not like I see it and then calmly decide I’m scared. It’s immediate, before I’ve even really thought about it. My chest sort of tightens up right away, and my hands start shaking. Sometimes I just freeze where I am, usually in the doorway if I’ve spotted one in a room, like I can’t make myself take another step. Other times I back away so fast it feels almost automatic, like my body has made the decision before my brain has caught up. It’s embarrassing, but yes, it’s definitely a sudden surge of fear.
Is your fear mainly limited to spiders?

Yes, mainly spiders. I mean, I can be startled by other bugs like anyone else, but it’s spiders that do this particular thing to me. And I know, logically, a spider sitting in the corner of an old house probably isn’t going to hurt me. I can say that perfectly sensibly right now, sitting here.

But the moment I imagine one dropping out of a box, or being near the washer when I’m reaching in, it suddenly feels… huge, somehow. Not physically huge, necessarily, but threatening, like it takes up the whole room in my mind. And I feel ridiculous saying that, because I know how it sounds, but yes — it’s really spiders specifically.
